source_user: Explain how quantization interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Quantization can reduce resident weight memory and memory traffic by representing weights or activations with fewer bits plus scale metadata. Mechanism: a weight-only int4 GEMM loads compact codes and applies group scales while accumulating products in FP16 or FP32, potentially reducing bandwidth and allowing a larger batch. Boundary: this does not guarantee lower end-to-end latency or higher throughput; dequantization, unsupported kernels, activation/KV-cache traffic, launch overhead, or a different batch regime may dominate. Compare matched model, hardware, software, prompt/output lengths, concurrency, and quality, and measure prefill/decode latency tails, throughput, memory high-water mark, and fallback time.
risks: Benefits depend on which tensors are quantized, scale granularity, calibration, kernels, and workload phase.
Nominal bit width omits scales, workspace, conversions, KV-cache, and fallback costs.
evidence_required: Bit format, tensor coverage, scale/outlier policy, accumulator type, kernel/runtime, hardware, and workload cells.
Matched quality results plus prefill/decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, memory, kernel/conversion breakdown, and fallback counts.

source_user: Explain how quantization interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Lower-precision storage generally reduces bytes moved for covered tensors, which can lower memory pressure and increase feasible concurrency. Mechanism: a fused low-bit matrix-multiply reads quantized codes, applies per-channel or per-group scales, and accumulates in a wider precision without materializing a full-precision weight matrix. Boundary: the gain is phase- and shape-dependent: decode may remain limited by KV-cache reads or launch overhead, while small shapes may not use an optimized low-bit kernel. Evaluate fixed prompt and generation lengths across batch/concurrency cells and report phase-specific latency, tokens/s, memory high-water mark, quality, and fallback events.
risks: Weight savings may not reduce total serving memory when activations, KV cache, metadata, or workspace dominate.
Kernel efficiency can vary by shape, device, batch, and precision path.
evidence_required: Quantized tensor inventory, scale representation, kernel coverage, device/software versions, and batch/length matrix.
Repeated prefill/decode measurements with confidence intervals or variance, memory accounting, throughput, quality regression checks, and failures.

source_user: Explain how quantization interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Quantization trades representation fidelity and conversion work for lower storage and bandwidth. Mechanism: groupwise scales map int8 or int4 codes to values consumed by a higher-precision accumulator, so a supported GEMM can fetch fewer weight bytes and reduce weight-memory footprint. Boundary: an apparent memory reduction may not translate to throughput if the workload is compute-bound, if only weights are quantized, or if conversions and fallback operations are on the critical path; quality can also regress from clipping or outliers. Use the same checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime, hardware, quality target, lengths, and concurrency, then measure latency distributions, throughput, memory by component, and numerical quality.
risks: The bottleneck can move from weight bandwidth to compute, activations, KV cache, or scheduling.
Calibration and outlier handling can make quality effects layer- and workload-specific.
evidence_required: Bottleneck profile, tensor coverage, quantization/calibration configuration, accumulator precision, and kernel path.
Matched baseline measurements for quality, component memory, prefill/decode latency tails, throughput, and conversion/fallback overhead.

source_user: Explain how quantization interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Quantization can lower weight memory and memory bandwidth, potentially permitting a larger batch or model on a device. Mechanism: a low-bit kernel consumes packed weight codes with scale/zero-point metadata and accumulates in FP16/FP32, avoiding a full-width weight load. Boundary: storage savings are not equal to end-to-end serving savings: KV-cache and activations may remain high precision, and conversion, metadata, kernel fallback, or synchronization can increase latency. Benchmark an unquantized reference and quantized candidate at identical prompt/output lengths, concurrency, hardware, and quality threshold; separate prefill from decode and record p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, memory high-water mark, and fallback counts.
risks: Partial quantization can leave the dominant memory or bandwidth consumer unchanged.
A larger feasible batch can improve aggregate throughput while worsening tail latency or quality.
evidence_required: Tensor coverage, metadata/workspace accounting, kernel support, batch policy, quality metric, and target service-level limits.
Matched phase-specific latency/throughput/memory results across concurrency, plus quality, fallback, and failure measurements.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether quantization helps a serving workload. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Define a matched baseline using the same model checkpoint, tokenizer, device, runtime, batching policy, prompt/output-length distribution, concurrency, and sampling settings; vary only quantization and its required kernel path. Mechanism to verify: profile whether packed low-bit weights plus fused scale application reduce weight bytes and memory stalls in GEMMs. Sweep short/long contexts and representative batch/concurrency cells, warm up, repeat randomized trials, and report prefill and decode p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, device-memory high-water mark by component, kernel/conversion time, and fallback events. Check task quality and error/timeout rates against a predeclared threshold. Boundary: a win in one phase or batch cell does not establish a production-wide win, especially if quantization coverage or quality differs.
risks: Unmatched workload or warm-up state can confound latency and throughput comparisons.
Quality regressions, unsupported shapes, and tail failures may be hidden by averages.
evidence_required: Predeclared workload cells, quality/error thresholds, quantization coverage, kernel inventory, and trial/repetition protocol.
Raw phase timings, tail statistics with variability, memory breakdown, profiler evidence, quality evaluation, and failure logs.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether quantization helps a serving workload. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: First freeze the reference and candidate configuration: identical checkpoint, software, device, request mix, prompt and output lengths, concurrency, batch scheduler, and quality acceptance rule. Measure baseline and quantized systems under the same warm-up and randomized order. Inspect the mechanism with profiler counters and kernel traces: determine whether low-bit loads and on-the-fly scaling reduce bytes or stalls, and account for dequantization and fallback kernels. Run enough repetitions for stable p50/p95/p99 prefill/decode latency, tokens/s, queueing delay, memory high-water mark, quality, timeouts, and errors. Boundary: extrapolation from a single batch size or from weight memory alone is invalid; include the actual production range and report uncertainty.
risks: Queueing, scheduler behavior, and request-length skew can change the observed service result.
Profiler overhead and insufficient repetitions can distort tail measurements.
evidence_required: Production-like request distribution, controlled randomization, repetition count, profiler configuration, and quality/error criteria.
Per-request and aggregate latency/throughput, memory components, kernel traces/counters, quality scores, and uncertainty.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether quantization helps a serving workload. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Construct a full-factorial or representative matrix over prompt length, generated length, batch/concurrency, and request mix. Hold model, tokenizer, hardware, runtime, scheduler, and service settings constant, and compare a full-precision reference with the quantized candidate in randomized runs after warm-up. Attribute any change using traces: low-bit GEMMs should show reduced weight traffic if the kernel applies scales during accumulation, while conversion, activation, and KV-cache traffic must be measured separately. Record prefill/decode p50/p95/p99 latency, queueing, throughput, memory high-water mark and components, quality, errors, and fallbacks. Boundary: quantization is acceptable only if the measured quality and reliability limits hold across the specified matrix; a mean speedup on a favorable cell is insufficient.
risks: A narrow benchmark can select for a favorable kernel shape and miss production regressions.
Quality and reliability constraints may trade off against throughput gains.
evidence_required: Workload matrix, matched reference, quantization coverage/configuration, acceptance thresholds, and randomization protocol.
Per-cell repeated results, phase/tail metrics, memory breakdown, profiler attribution, quality evaluation, and failure counts.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether quantization helps a serving workload. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Specify success before testing: a quality/error tolerance, a service-level tail-latency limit, and the throughput and memory metrics to optimize. Establish an unquantized baseline, then deploy the candidate with identical hardware, software, request distribution, lengths, concurrency, and batching. Use kernel traces and memory counters to test the mechanism—packed weights and fused scale application should reduce covered weight traffic, but quantify dequantization, metadata, workspace, activations, and KV cache. Repeat each workload cell and report prefill/decode latency quantiles, throughput, queueing, memory high-water mark, quality, timeouts, and fallback/unsupported-operation counts. Boundary: do not claim a general benefit if only one device, shape, phase, or calibration set was tested.
risks: Optimizing one metric can violate quality, tail-latency, or reliability requirements.
Calibration-set mismatch and device-specific kernel support can invalidate generalization.
evidence_required: Predeclared acceptance criteria, baseline/candidate configs, device and runtime details, and calibration data description.
Repeated phase-specific tails, throughput, queueing, component memory, quality, kernel/counter evidence, and failures.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether quantization helps a serving workload. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: Use a paired benchmark with the same checkpoint, tokenizer, request traces, prompt/output lengths, concurrency, scheduler, device, runtime, and sampling parameters. Warm both systems, randomize test order, and repeat enough trials to quantify variance. Collect per-request and aggregate prefill/decode latency, queueing delay, tokens/s, memory high-water mark by weights/activations/KV/workspace, kernel and conversion time, fallback events, errors, and task-quality metrics. Mechanism: correlate any gain with reduced bytes or stalls from packed-weight GEMMs and fused scaling rather than infer causality from bit width. Boundary: accept the result only within the tested workload and stated quality/reliability thresholds; extrapolation across shapes or phases requires new evidence.
risks: Systematic benchmark ordering, cache state, or thermal effects can bias paired results.
Average throughput can hide tail-latency, error-rate, or quality regressions.
evidence_required: Paired/randomized trial design, production-like traces, quantization/kernel coverage, quality and reliability thresholds.
Raw per-request data, repeated summary statistics, memory components, profiler attribution, quality results, and failure logs.

source_user: What assumptions must be stated before making a performance claim about quantization? Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Quantization reduces representation precision and often memory traffic, but accuracy, kernel support, calibration, and outlier handling must be measured.
corrected_answer: State the model/checkpoint and tokenizer, tensors and layers quantized, bit format, scale granularity, zero-point/outlier policy, accumulator precision, calibration data, and quality metric. Also state hardware, software/runtime and kernel versions, batch/concurrency policy, prompt/output-length distribution, sampling, warm-up, and whether the claim concerns prefill, decode, or end-to-end serving. Mechanism: lower-bit weights plus scale metadata can reduce GEMM weight bytes and memory pressure when a supported kernel consumes them efficiently. Boundary: this is conditional, not a bit-width law; unsupported shapes, conversion overhead, unquantized activations/KV cache, or quality loss can erase the claimed benefit. Require matched measurements of latency tails, throughput, memory, quality, and failures before generalizing.
risks: Omitting tensor coverage, calibration, or kernel details makes comparisons non-reproducible.
A phase-specific or device-specific result may be incorrectly presented as an end-to-end general claim.
evidence_required: Complete model, quantization, calibration, hardware/software, workload, and metric specification.
Matched reference measurements with phase/tail latency, throughput, memory, quality, kernel coverage, and failure evidence.
